top_categories.workout_context: 13,543ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 107, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
127ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Granfondo La Fausto Coppi, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo La Fausto Coppi's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Granfondo La Fausto Coppi. Practice on paved Italian mountain roads through the Maritime: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 107 miles.
13,543ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo La Fausto Coppi. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 107 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,543ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 13,543ft of climbing on paved Italian mountain roads through the Maritime does to your power file on race day.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo La Fausto Coppi. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Granfondo La Fausto Coppi’s 107 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Granfondo La Fausto Coppi includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. Summit temperatures at Colle Fauniera (2,481m) can drop to 8-12C even in late June — a 15-18C differential from the valley start.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Granfondo La Fausto Coppi rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved italian mountain roads through the maritime alps and piedmont foothills to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Durability, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 107 miles of paved italian mountain roads through the maritime alps and piedmont foothills in Cuneo, Piedmont, Italy.
